steps.title: The possessor and the possessed thing
steps.body: In the simple possession pattern shown here, the possessor after the possession preposition is genitive. The thing possessed is nominative. The schematic slot in the first example represents that possessed thing. У меня есть Х — I have X. У вас есть сын? — Do you have a son?

steps.title: Possession versus absence
steps.body: A simple positive possession line places the possessed thing in the nominative. An absence line places the absent thing in the genitive. Decide whether the whole shown line affirms or denies possession.

steps.title: Positive statements and questions
steps.body: The son examples keep the same simple possession pattern in a statement or question: genitive possessor and nominative possessed thing. The form of a question does not turn the noun into an absence construction. Да, у меня есть сын. — Yes, I have a son. У твоего́ му́жа есть оди́н друг — Your husband has one friend.

steps.title: Keep quantity and absence separate
steps.body: The many-friends example includes a quantity expression. Quantity patterns are separate from the simple nominative possessed thing in the son checks. The no-son example below denies possession and uses the genitive for the absent thing. У моего нового мужа есть много друзе́й — My new husband has many friends. У меня́ нет сы́на — No, I don't have a son.

steps.title: Another absence example
steps.body: The no-money example also denies possession. Choose the genitive absence explanation, rather than the simple positive possession explanation. У моего́ бра́та нет де́нег — My brother doesn't have any money.

steps.title: Guided practice
steps.body: Read the whole shown line, then choose the complete case explanation. A missed check returns to all teaching and examples.

steps.title: Identify absence
steps.body: In an absence line, the absent thing is genitive. An absence line may describe what a person does not have or what does not exist at a place. У меня́ нет сы́на — No, I don't have a son. Нет рестора́нов — There are no restaurants.

steps.title: Choose a complete case explanation
steps.body: The absence construction uses a genitive noun for the absent thing. The simple positive possession construction instead uses a genitive possessor and a nominative possessed thing. Choose from the meaning and construction of the whole supplied line.

steps.title: Apply the absence pattern
steps.body: Both negative examples below use the genitive for the absent thing. Keep the absent thing separate from any possessor or place mentioned in the line. В Москве́ нет ста́рых зда́ний — There are no old buildings in Moscow. У моего́ бра́та нет де́нег — My brother doesn't have any money.

steps.title: Compare with positive possession
steps.body: The positive son example below affirms possession. Its possessed noun is nominative, so the genitive absence explanation does not classify this line. Да, у меня есть сын. — Yes, I have a son.

steps.title: Admitted lines

steps.title: Admitted instruction
steps.body: For a regular verb, the past tense removes -ть and adds -л, with gender endings. Irregulars such as идти and the past of быть are outside that recipe and must be learned as listed forms.
